similar_scenes.name: Pub rock y primeros indies
similar_scenes.book: Postpunk. Romper todo y empezar de nuevo
similar_scenes.author: Simon Reynolds
similar_scenes.desc: Justo antes del punk nacen Chiswick (Count Bishops, 1975) y Stiff (Nick Lowe, 1976), sellos independientes surgidos del pub rock pero dirigidos por veteranos de la industria que enseguida se asocian con las distribuidoras grandes: Stiff se convierte en la máquina de hits new wave de Ian Dury y Elvis Costello.
similar_scenes.family: Antecedentes: punk, art rock, kraut y glam

similar_scenes.name: British Graffiti: pub-rock y mods
similar_scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
similar_scenes.desc: Gran Bretaña tenía los pubs: el renacimiento nace de los músicos que tocaban rhythm'n'blues y rockabilly en ellos, y el punk les saca de allí. Surge un nuevo cantautor, anclado en las raíces y consciente de lo social: Dave Edmunds, Nick Lowe, Graham Parker, Joe Jackson, Elvis Costello (el «joven airado» de la new wave, quizá sobrevalorado), Tom Robinson, Ian Dury, Wreckless Eric. Dire Straits; el revival mod de los Jam y los Television Personalities; los Soft Boys de Robyn Hitchcock, cimiento del revival psicodélico; Boomtown Rats, Undertones, Bananarama.

podcast.title: Characteristics and Scene
podcast.body: Pub rock comprised a tight network of British bands that wore denim and other "glam-free outfits," performing home-spun rock and roll in small clubs around the London area. These bands explicitly rejected album-oriented rock, favoring songs typically two to three minutes in length, and played with a "proto-punk economy." "A tight network of British bands dressed in denim and other glam-free outfits, playing home spun rock and roll in small London area clubs."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Foundation for "Angry Young Men"
podcast.body: Pub Rock served as a foundational scene for British singer-songwriters like Elvis Costello, Joe Jackson, and Graham Parker in the 1970s. It was part of the musical landscape that shaped their early careers before they adopted punk attitudes and contributed to new wave. "who came up through Pub Rock and Powerpop, adopted punk attitude, helped shape new wave."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Incubator of Talent
podcast.body: The greater London pub rock scene served as an incubator for several key artists, including Nick Lowe and Elvis Costello. "Costello made his way through the greater London pub rock scene, the same scene that incubated Nick Low."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Nick Lowe's Origins
podcast.body: The British pub rock scene of the early 1970s was the formative environment for Nick Lowe, a key figure in Powerpop. This scene provided the foundation for his distinct sound and songwriting approach. "One of the British Godfathers of this sound was Nick Lowe, a guy who came out of the British pubroxene of the early 70s..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Origin of "Angry Young Men"
podcast.body: The "Angry Young Men" movement, encompassing artists like Elvis Costello, Joe Jackson, and Graham Parker, significantly grew out of England's pub rock and punk rock scenes, as well as the transatlantic sound of Power Pop. "Growing out of England's pub rock and punk rock scenes."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Pre-Punk Scene (1970s Britain)
podcast.body: Pub rock was a significant scene in England prior to the full explosion of punk rock. Bands like The 101ers (from which Joe Strummer defected) and Brimsley Schwartz were prominent in this genre. "I remember at the time, the big thing going on in England was Paw Brock. Dr. Philgit was the big band at the time in Brimsley Schwartz."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Prominence in 1970s England
podcast.body: When the Ramones visited England in 1976, pub rock was "the big thing going on," with bands like Dr. Feelgood and Brinsley Schwarz being prominent. "I remember at the time the big thing going on in England was Pobrock, Dr. Felga, was the big band at the time in Brimsley Schwartz."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rejection of Hippy Rock
podcast.body: The pub rock genre was conceived as a deliberate rejection of the sounds and ideals of 1960s hippie rock. "The pub rock genre was intended as a rejection of 60's hippy rock."
